newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: RALLYING-MAKINEN SET FOR PORTUGUESE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN SET FOR PORTUGUESE VICTORY.

text.p: Reigning world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland looked set for his first victory of the season in the Rally of Portugal on Tuesday.
The Mitsubishi driver's only real rival for the win, Kenneth Eriksson in the Subaru, dropped out with mechanical problems near the end of the second leg.

Makinen, who had been locked in a thrilling battle with the Swedish driver for most of the day, had pulled out a 32-second lead by the end of the 21st stage when Eriksson's car broke down on the 22nd, the final of the day, with an engine problem.
"Until the team gets to look at the car, we are not sure exactly what caused the failure," said a Subaru spokeswoman. "But it was definitely a mechanical problem and not an electrical problem."

Eriksson's retirement, which came after a day when he had been delayed by spectators crowding the stages on the 20th stage, means that Makinen now leads the rally by more than three minutes from Belgian Freddy Loix heading into the final day on Wednesday.

A victory for the Finn would hand him the lead in the world championship following a disappointing start to the season where he has just claimed two third-place finishes from the opening three rounds on the calendar.

The Portuguese event, which had claimed the two world championship leaders, Colin McRae of Britain and Carlos Sainz of Spain, on its opening day, also saw front-runner Mitsubishi's Richard Burns retire on Tuesday afternoon.
The Briton had been running in a strong fourth position when he encountered gearbox problems on the road section between the 16th and 17th stages.
"It's very disappointing," he said. "The gearbox started making worrying noises on stage 15 and, by stage 16, I started losing gears altogether.
"Then the transmission failed completely before the start of stage 17 and, with no servicing allowed, we had to accept defeat."

The retirement of the leading drivers has also proved a benefit to German Armin Schwarz in the Ford, the only other championship contender, who now lies third in the rally after recovering from an accident on the first day.
